A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same peer-review detection benchmark and Anchor method. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original detector evaluations, AI-editing experiments, qualitative review analysis, and statistical comparisons of human and AI review scores.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds prompt-variation experiments, bootstrap uncertainty estimates, and computation-time measurements.

M1.justification: The anchor-generation prompt, embedding comparison, thresholding equations, and three-anchor OR voting remain unchanged. v1 Section 4 becomes v2 Section 5.1 and Appendix D.1; the context-aware terminology does not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: The underlying ICLR/NeurIPS coverage and five generating LLMs remain unchanged. v2 adds a limited test scenario involving 1,921 GPT-4o reviews of ICLR 2021 papers generated with alternative reviewer-archetype prompts, extending coverage to prompt-induced variation.

E2.justification: Corresponding detection tables retain the same comparator membership, and the editing study still compares Anchor with Binoculars. MFD's description is corrected, but its citation and reported implementation source remain the same; no changed evaluated implementation is established. v1's commercial-API claim has no identifiable corresponding reported comparison.

E3.justification: v2 explicitly restricts main evaluations to pre-2023 reviews, whereas v1 describes using the withheld test set spanning through 2024. Unchanged headline scores leave unclear whether this reflects rerunning or clarified reporting. The editing evaluation now reports two target-FPR settings, replacing one unspecified-threshold presentation. New protocols also evaluate cross-prompt transfer at fixed calibration thresholds and processing time for 100 samples under specified GPU/API conditions.

E4.justification: v2 adds a substantive investigation of prompt sensitivity through cross-prompt detection tests and embedding/t-SNE analysis (Section 5.2, Appendix D.2). It also revises the editing-sensitivity evaluation and adds an efficiency analysis. The existing editing-similarity validation, human review examples, score comparisons, and alternative-calibration analysis are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 reports Wilcoxon tests for review-score differences but no uncertainty estimates for its main detection table. v2 adds standard deviations from 100 bootstrap resamples across those detection results (Table S5), plus means and standard deviations from 20 timing repetitions (Figure S1). These are resampling and timing repetitions, not evidence of additional independent training runs.

E6.justification: The headline detection table, ROC curves, and review-score histograms are unchanged. However, Table 10 becomes S7 with Anchor's Llama TPR at 0.1% target FPR changing from 12.2% to 13.6%; its Qwen FPR/TPR at 1% target changes from 1.0%/88.1% to 1.3%/92.1%. The editing table replaces results, changes Anchor/Binoculars NDCG from 0.98/0.94 to 0.90/0.86, and removes the fully generated column. Prompt-transfer and runtime outcomes are added. These changes do not establish general same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and their mathematical content are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs, and v2 introduces no substantive mathematical derivation or formal assumption.

C1.justification: v2 moderates the broad superiority claim in v1's abstract and contribution list, presenting Anchor as a context-aware approach with strong performance under strict FPR constraints. The main benchmark contribution, difficulty of low-FPR detection, and claimed advantage for GPT-4o and Claude reviews remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets its prompt tests as evidence of stable review distributions and generalization, and emphasizes difficulty detecting light editing. It adds concrete limitations concerning humans editing AI drafts, API cost/scalability, and anchor-model selection. Existing interpretations of review specificity, inflated scores, and weak Anchor performance on Llama are retained.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a concrete dataset address and names the Intel OBL Internal R&D Use License Agreement, beyond v1's general release statements. It adds exact archetype prompts, embedding/t-SNE settings, timing hardware/API details, and identification of the editing subset. These extend reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to retained implementations.

R1.justification: v2 adds Li et al. (2025) on perturbation robustness and D'Arcy et al. (2024) on MARG, and revises its characterization of Latona et al.'s use of proprietary detection solutions. Most cited work and the positioning around individual-review detection remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative around benchmarking followed by question-based analyses. Anchor moves from a standalone methodology section into the analysis section, voting moves to the appendix, and editing material is consolidated. Limitations precede the conclusion, ethics moves to the appendix, and the abstract, contribution list, and conclusion are rewritten. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column formatting, with extensive table resizing and relocation. v2 restructures the editing table into two FPR blocks, adds uncertainty and prompt-comparison tables, and introduces runtime and t-SNE figures. Figure 1 is relabeled, while the existing ROC and score-distribution graphics are reused.

improvement.justification: v2 improves scrutiny and usability through bootstrap uncertainty, prompt-transfer testing, explicit low-FPR editing results, timing information, and concrete dataset access details. Its claims and limitations are also better qualified. The gain remains limited: prompt robustness covers one model/year, and the newly stated temporal restriction and revised editing results are not fully reconciled with the earlier reporting.
